conclusions.rationale: The actual specification bounds library size and Unicode-length validation, names CRUD and confirmation, and requires restart persistence; it supplies a testable feature contract without new unapproved scope.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The settings UI lists prompts with name, provider (default or override) and shortcut, and supports create, edit and delete with confirmation. A prompt is valid when its trimmed name has 1–60 characters and is unique case-insensitively, and its text has 1–8000 characters. The library holds at most 50 prompts. Changes persist across restarts.

conclusions.rationale: The current specification retains all old prompts and selection, flags invalid legacy values without deleting them and bounds once-only starter addition; technical migration policy can meet it.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** On upgrade, existing prompts and the existing selected prompt are kept unchanged, and the starter prompts Minimal correction, Friendly rephrasing, Clarify, Shorten, Notes and Translate to English are added once when absent by name; they are editable and deletable. Starter prompts are added only while the library has room under its limit. Existing prompts that break the new validation rules are kept, flagged invalid and cannot be used until edited.

conclusions.rationale: Enable/None/default/three-trigger semantics and recording-only selection are defined, with measurable 200 ms and focus-preservation targets across indicator platforms; native feasibility remains evidence to produce.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The existing "AI post-processing" switch keeps its meaning: when off, no dictation is processed, prompt shortcuts are unregistered and the indicator menu is hidden. When on, settings define one default prompt or "None". The plain dictation shortcut starts with "None", the post-processing shortcut with the default prompt, and a prompt shortcut with its prompt. While a dictation is recording, the indicator shows the prompt for this dictation and offers a menu listing "None" and every prompt; a choice applies to this dictation only and does not change the default. The menu opens within 200 ms without taking keyboard focus from the user's application, on every platform where the indicator is shown.

conclusions.rationale: Default routing versus complete per-prompt provider/model override, existing provider scope and not-ready skip reasons are specified; keys remain provider-owned.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Each prompt uses the default provider and model unless it defines a provider and model override. Providers are the existing ones, including the local custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint and, where available, Apple Intelligence. A prompt whose provider lacks a required endpoint, model or API key is shown as not ready with the missing item; processing with it skips the AI step.

conclusions.rationale: All failure classes and total deadline are explicit, including four-second notification and raw/name/reason retention. Cancellation preserves existing history behavior rather than introducing a new rollback promise.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** When the AI step fails (provider or HTTP error, empty or whitespace-only result, provider not ready) or the whole step, including any internal retry or fallback request, exceeds 30 seconds, the initial transcript is inserted, the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that processing failed and the original was inserted, and the history keeps the initial transcript, the prompt name and the failure reason. Cancelling during processing inserts nothing; history behaves as today for cancelled dictations.

conclusions.rationale: Shortcut count, global activation semantics, sole 004 checker and confirmed-delete cleanup are explicit; owner integration is required rather than a new conflict engine.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** A prompt may have 0–2 shortcuts. A prompt shortcut starts a dictation processed with that prompt and follows the global activation mode. Prompt shortcuts use the shared conflict checker of feature 004 against every other shortcut. Deleting a prompt removes its shortcuts after confirmation.

conclusions.rationale: The editable sample/result metadata and 30-second bound are measurable and insertion/history effects are expressly excluded.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The test panel runs a prompt on editable sample text (prefilled with the last transcript when one exists) and shows the result, provider, model and duration, or the error, within the 30-second limit. A test never inserts text into another application and never writes history.

conclusions.rationale: Every required prompt operation and override clear is specified alongside 004 shortcut ownership, JSON-only envelope and credential exclusion from every output channel.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) offers prompt list, create, update, delete, set-default and set-provider-override (provider id and model, or `--clear` to return to the default provider); prompt shortcuts are managed with the shortcut operations of feature 004. Outputs never contain API keys, in stdout, stderr or logs; provider readiness is reported as ready or the missing item. With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope; errors use stable codes.

conclusions.rationale: Stable entity identity, validated library, optional atomic routing override, bounded shortcut projection and non-destructive once-only migration map to explicit acceptance criteria.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Persist a validated prompt library with stable ids, names, texts, optional provider/model override and 0–2 shortcuts; migrate existing prompts and add starter prompts once.

conclusions.rationale: Trigger selection and acknowledged recording choice define runtime session semantics without changing persistent default.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Resolve the prompt of each dictation from its trigger (plain, post-processing or prompt shortcut) and from a per-dictation choice made on the indicator, without changing the default.

conclusions.rationale: The single whole-step budget explicitly contains readiness work, retries/fallback requests and resolved provider/model routing; pure readiness and injected clients support tests.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Run the AI step with the prompt's resolved provider and model, report provider readiness, and bound the whole step, including internal retries and fallback requests, to 30 seconds.

conclusions.rationale: Raw fallback, failure recording and cancellation are observable requirements; retention independent of audio is a necessary implementation consequence.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Insert the initial transcript and record the failure whenever the AI step does not produce a valid result; respect cancellation.

conclusions.rationale: Prompt testing is scoped to results and errors with no external insertion or history writes.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Provide a test operation that never inserts text or writes history.

conclusions.rationale: Read/mutate/default/override operations are named and linked to CLI credential secrecy; transport details remain 008 authority.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Expose prompt read and modify operations, including setting and clearing the per-prompt provider/model override, through the settings CLI without ever outputting API keys.

conclusions.rationale: Enumerated fault injections have a quantitative original-text/recorded-failure target; insertion proof remains distinct from provider fallback and cannot be inferred from dispatch.

source_citations.excerpt: In fault-injection tests (provider error, HTTP error, timeout of the whole step, empty result, not ready), 100% of dictations insert the initial transcript and record the failure.

conclusions.rationale: Exact zero key occurrences across CLI output/logs is a meaningful measurable negative criterion including errors.

source_citations.excerpt: Secret scanning of CLI outputs and logs across all prompt operations finds zero API key occurrences.

conclusions.rationale: Exact prompt/text/selected-id preservation gives a measurable upgrade invariant without destructive normalization.

source_citations.excerpt: Upgrading a store with custom prompts keeps all prompts, texts and the selected prompt unchanged.

findings.description: Text retention must remain durable if WAV saving fails; current audio-gated storage cannot certify the required raw/name/reason history.
findings.suggestion: Plan a real text-only migration and fault-injected reread, preserving the existing cancellation boundary.

citations.excerpt: the history keeps the initial transcript, the prompt name and the failure reason

findings.description: A browser-only check cannot establish menu latency and absence of native keyboard-focus transfer.
findings.suggestion: Require early nonactivating host spike and per-platform release observations.

citations.excerpt: The menu opens within 200 ms without taking keyboard focus from the user's application, on every platform where the indicator is shown.

findings.description: Concurrent edit/delete and stop require a consistent session snapshot rather than late lookup of partially changed provider data.
findings.suggestion: Serialize recording selection/stop and snapshot one revision; test late callbacks.

citations.excerpt: Dictation stops before the user picks in the menu: the prompt shown at stop time applies.

findings.description: The literal original-inserted notification cannot be certified from successful paste dispatch alone.
findings.suggestion: Retain actual target evidence and clarify runtime wording when verification is unknown.

citations.excerpt: the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that processing failed and the original was inserted

findings.description: Current source strategy has no cargo/native harness despite backend deadline, history and routing obligations.
findings.suggestion: Resolve Rust commands and injectable clients/clock/history/output, with manual native evidence separate.
